TASK-MIG-004.notes: Extracted one private durable-persistence utility (src/histgerm/research/_persistence.py) providing same-directory temporary write + flush + fsync + optional chmod (write_durable_temporary), atomic replace with prior-content-preserving cleanup (replace_atomically), temporary removal (remove_temporary), a deterministic external lock path (stable_lock_path), and a bounded OS-backed exclusive advisory lock (bounded_file_lock). ledger.py now delegates _lock_path_for_ledger/_ledger_file_lock/_write_temporary/_commit to the shared utility while preserving the ledger's OS lock (namespace 'ledger-locks-v1'), revision guards, LedgerWriteError/LedgerRevisionError/LedgerPolicyError types, and byte-stable canonical YAML. vocabulary_store.py replaces the fragile O_CREAT|O_EXCL next-to-file lock with the same OS advisory lock (namespace 'vocabulary-locks-v1'): a crashed owner leaves no stale lock because the kernel releases the advisory lock on process exit, giving explicit stale-owner handling without unsafe automatic deletion, and no next-to-file .lock is ever created. discovery_protocol.write_checkpoint now flushes and fsyncs the checkpoint through the shared utility while keeping the 0o600 permissions, '.histgerm-' temp prefix, MAX_CHECKPOINT_BYTES bound, DiscoveryProtocolError size error, and original-exception re-raise on OS failure. No serialized ledger/vocabulary/checkpoint format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed. New robust tests cover fsync durability, atomic-replace prior-content preservation, cross-process ledger and vocabulary revision contention without lost updates, bounded-lock timeout against a live owner, and stale-owner lock reclaim after an owner crash with no lock-file deletion. No live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.

TASK-MIG-005.notes: Reworked bounded, transient model-led elicitation (src/histgerm/research/elicitation.py) so malformed model output is recovered candidate-locally instead of discarding valid work. The whole-response candidate list is now parsed independently of the candidates it contains (_ResponseEnvelope validates only the {"candidates": [...]} envelope with extra='forbid'/strict), and each candidate is validated on its own via _CandidateOutput: one malformed sibling (extra field, URL/control-char name, wrong type, non-object entry) becomes a scoped ElicitationQuarantine (scope='candidate', deterministic 1-based position, stable reason, best-effort raw name) while every valid sibling is retained. Invalid response formatting (non-JSON, wrong envelope shape, a non-list candidates value, or oversize output) is retried exactly once with a schema-feedback prompt that echoes the exact rejection reason and re-states the name-only contract; a recovered retry yields leads and after retry exhaustion the response becomes a scope='response' quarantine that contributes no leads (no success-shaped fallback). Safe count-limit excess is truncated with an explicit warning: max_candidates_per_response drops surplus entries and max_aliases_per_candidate trims surplus aliases while keeping the lead. Deterministic ElicitationMetrics (retries_attempted/recovered, responses_blocked, candidates_quarantined, candidates_truncated, aliases_truncated) and warnings/quarantines are exposed on ElicitationResult as additive, default-valued fields (existing leads/prompts/requires_external_search unchanged), ElicitationPrompt.kind widens to include 'retry', and ElicitationOutputError stays exported and is still raised loudly when the injected model returns a non-string (a dependency-contract violation, never a recoverable model formatting error). DiscoveryCoverage gains elicitation_retries/recovered_retries/blocked_responses/quarantined_candidates counters surfaced through snapshot() and DiscoveryRunResult.as_json, wired from ElicitationResult.metrics in run_discovery. Provider-gap and trusted-evidence semantics are untouched (elicitation still produces only untrusted name-only leads requiring external search). New/updated tests cover malformed arrays, malformed objects/siblings, URL/wrong-type names, invalid-JSON-then-valid retry recovery, repeated-invalid scoped blocking, candidate- and alias-count truncation warnings, oversize retry recovery, non-string loud rejection, the surviving exclusion-name bound, the new metrics snapshot keys, and an end-to-end run_discovery worker-result path that keeps a valid lead beside a quarantined sibling and surfaces the metrics. No serialized ledger/vocabulary/checkpoint format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed; no live ledger/vocabulary/inventory YAML changed.

persistence.description: Shared durable, atomic, single-writer persistence primitives extracted for TASK-MIG-004 and reused by the ledger, vocabulary store, and checkpoint writer.
primitives: write_durable_temporary: same-directory mkstemp, write, flush, os.fsync, optional chmod; cleans up and re-raises the original error on failure.
replace_atomically: os.replace with prior-content-preserving cleanup that re-raises the original error so the caller reports its own atomic-replace failure.
remove_temporary: unlink tolerating only prior absence.
stable_lock_path: deterministic per-target lock path outside the target directory, distinct per target and namespace.
bounded_file_lock: bounded OS-backed exclusive advisory lock on a never-evicted lock file; the kernel releases it on owner exit so a crash leaves no stale lock and no unsafe deletion is required.

consumers.ledger: namespace 'ledger-locks-v1'; preserves LedgerWriteError/LedgerRevisionError/LedgerPolicyError and byte-stable canonical YAML.
consumers.vocabulary: namespace 'vocabulary-locks-v1'; replaces the O_CREAT|O_EXCL next-to-file lock, so no '.<name>.lock' is created and a crashed owner is handled without deletion.
consumers.checkpoint: adds flush + os.fsync while keeping 0o600 permissions, the '.histgerm-' temp prefix, the size bound, and original-exception re-raise on OS failure.

persistence.serialization_diff: none: no ledger, vocabulary, or checkpoint serialized format, public exception type, or CLI exit code changed, so no artifact hash is required for this task.

elicitation_recovery.description: Candidate-local model-output recovery for TASK-MIG-005: malformed sibling output never discards valid candidate leads, and unrecoverable output becomes an explicit, deterministic quarantine instead of an exception or a success-shaped fallback.
primitives: _ResponseEnvelope: validates only the {"candidates": [...]} envelope (extra='forbid', strict) so individual candidates are parsed independently; a non-JSON body, wrong envelope shape, non-list candidates value, or oversize output is returned as a soft _EnvelopeError, never a raise.

_elicit_response: retries invalid response formatting exactly once with a schema-feedback prompt (ElicitationPrompt kind='retry') that echoes the exact rejection reason; a recovered retry yields leads, and after retry exhaustion the response becomes a scope='response' ElicitationQuarantine contributing no leads.

_add_output_leads: validates each candidate via _CandidateOutput; a malformed sibling becomes a scope='candidate' ElicitationQuarantine (deterministic 1-based position, stable reason, best-effort raw name) while valid siblings are retained; max_candidates_per_response and max_aliases_per_candidate excess is truncated with an explicit warning.
_call_model: raises the still-exported ElicitationOutputError only when the injected model returns a non-string (a dependency-contract violation, never a recoverable model formatting error).
